name: Mount Sharp Boxwork Ridges
finding: Observed crisscrossing mineral-cemented bedrock fracture ridges standing 1–2 m tall across Mount Sharp; interpreted as evidence that ancient groundwater table remained high late into Gale Crater's history.

source.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Explores a 'Spiderweb' on Mars

limitations: Exact pixel coordinates on active raster 'hirise-mro-pia26306-boxwork-2048x1042-v1' remain unavailable pending rover-to-orbital georeferencing.
Ancient groundwater cementation does not demonstrate current liquid water.

name: Vera Rubin Ridge Hematite & Calcium Sulfate Veins
finding: Measured crystalline hematite and crosscutting calcium sulfate mineral veins in layered lacustrine mudstone bedrock along Vera Rubin Ridge; records multiple episodes of diagenetic subsurface fluid alteration.

source.title: NASA Science — Curiosity's Proposed Path Up Mount Sharp

limitations: Measured along the Vera Rubin Ridge traverse; precise location on the PIA26306 boxwork frame is unavailable.
Ground truth fluid alteration at the ridge does not determine regional trafficability or hazard clearance.

name: Mount Sharp Sulfate-Bearing Unit Transition
finding: Derived stratigraphic mineral transition from clay-rich lakebed mudstones to salty sulfate-bearing layered strata; records a major planetary climate transition from wetter ancient lakes to drier conditions.
limitations: Spectroscopic and XRD detection of sulfate salts; exact pixel coordinates on the active raster are unavailable.
Regional paleoclimate transition does not provide route-level slope or hazard safety guarantees.
